content.text:
Henry Morton returns to Milnwood, enters the kitchen, and is recognized by Ailie. He later travels to Niel Blane’s inn, then to Widow Maclure’s cottage, where Peggy guides him to Burley’s refuge in the Black Linn. Burley destroys the legal deed, attacks Morton, and later dies while fleeing after Lord Evandale is ambushed and killed; Morton arrives with Dutch troops. Edith and Morton eventually marry, while Lady Margaret regains Tillietudlem and other characters receive happier fates.

The latter text recounts railroad disasters caused by weak brakes, telescoping cars, broken couplings, derailments, unsafe bridges, open draws, fires, and inadequate signaling. It emphasizes the Miller platform, Westinghouse brake, telegraph, automatic block systems, and interlocking switches as lifesaving improvements, while criticizing railroad conservatism and reliance on human vigilance.
